title: Nova acquires 80% of Stella
text: On 1 January N, Nova bought 80% of the shares of Stella for 1,500 K€ in cash. Stella has a customer list (not recognised in its own balance sheet) with a fair value of 300 K€. All other assets and liabilities: fair value = carrying amount. Goodwill is measured on the parent's share (partial goodwill); non-controlling interests are measured at their share of the fair value of Stella's identifiable net assets.

title: ShopCo – impairment of the Lyon store (a CGU)
text: ShopCo, a retail chain, tests each store as a cash-generating unit. Because of a sharp drop in sales in Lyon, the store is tested at 31 December N. The CGU's value in use is €1,050,000; its fair value less costs to sell is €980,000.

Carrying amount
Fair value less costs to sell

title: Novatel – leasing a hotel building
text: On 1 January N1 Novatel leases a hotel building for 5 years and decides how it is used. Payments: €100,000 at the end of each year. Interest rate implicit in the lease 5% (annuity factor 5%, 5 years = 4.3295). Novatel pays €7,050 of initial direct costs (legal fees) on 1 January N1. Straight-line depreciation over the lease term.

title: Orion – debt, equity and KPIs
text: Orion SA issues a convertible bond for €50,000,000 on 1 January N. The present value of its contractual cash flows at the market rate for similar non-convertible debt is €46,200,000.
Orion bought back 100,000 own shares at €20 in N−1. In N it resells 30,000 of them at €18.
Key figures N (million €): EBIT 2,400; depreciation and amortisation 600; tax rate 25%; capital employed 20,000; WACC 8%.
